page: Microsoft Azure DC16es_v5 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the DCEV5 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and features 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel processor. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. This configuration runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, ensuring dedicated CPU allocation for workloads requiring consistent compute performance.

This server type does not include any local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via external network-attached storage. It is, however, designated as Premium Storage capable, allowing integration with high-performance persistent disks. There are no integrated GPUs on this instance, and it does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the DC16es_v5 offers a balanced resource density within the Intel-based hardware class. Although classified under a memory-optimized family, the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio aligns closely with general-purpose specifications. This profile is suitable for enterprise applications, relational databases, middle-tier application servers, and structured data processing tasks that require dedicated CPU resources without the need for local scratch space.
